name: sunlight_init_default

Live-measured this session on two running levels with different on-disk Inclination (0x40/0x20): sunX=sunZ=sunBase=147 in both, turn 20 and turn 77 (9+ multiples of the 8-turn tick 0x401350 checks), confirming the level's own sunlight block never visibly moves the vector away from this flat default in normal play - see 0x401350/0x401920/0x4be230 - pop3-rev-analysis.md "Terrain land colour"

Called from 5 sites exe-wide (0x4032bc, 0x4036e1, 0x4038c6, 0x4038d1, 0x404be6, 0x4ba37d) - not yet traced individually, but given the sibling `landscape_set_unit_shadow`'s own call sites (building-placement-era code, see below), this is almost certainly "recompute this object's ground-shadow footprint whenever it moves/changes," i.e. the per-cell "ambient_nibble" compute_cell_light (0x4be230) reads is really an **object/building shadow intensity**, not a static light constant - resolves the contradiction between a live measurement (nonzero +0xe low nibble under a hill's temple) and pop3-rev-analysis.md's prior "nothing writes it, probably always 0" conclusion, which only looked at terrain-specific functions and missed this unit-movement-triggered writer - pop3-rev-analysis.md "Terrain land colour"

Found this session tracing `init_unit_building`'s (0x4036D0) preamble (its very first call). Computes the ground HEIGHT at a newly-placed building's own door point: resolves its shape/door-offset via the shape table (0x895ec1, indexed by the building's own shape id `+0x33`) and a 4-way facing switch (quantized from `+0x26`) to pick a rotated door-adjacent corner offset from the shared shape-data table (`0x59df3c+0x2c`, same table `landscape_set_unit_shadow`/0x403c10 and 0x403f00 below read for their own footprint walks), adds the building's own door-offset fields (`+0x7a`/`+0x7c`), clamps the result on-map (0x4ee580), samples ground height there via the universal terrain-height function (0x44e940, same one `compute_cell_light`'s docs already cite for `ground()`), and stores it into the building's own `+0x41` height field, clearing flag `+0x10` bit `0x400`. Not the same function as 0x4044b0 ("a building's door point", below) - this one goes one step further to also sample height, and was not checked this session for whether it literally calls 0x4044b0 internally or duplicates its math. Called from `init_unit_building` (0x4036D1) before the footprint shadow recompute (`landscape_move_1`, 0x403a00) - pop3-rev-analysis.md has no "building placement" write-up yet to attach this to.

Found this session, same `init_unit_building` (0x4036D0) preamble, called next (0x4036F0) for every building type EXCEPT 0xa (wall, `cmp [esi+0x2b],0xa`). Ground-flattening under a newly-placed building's footprint: walks the building's own footprint cells (same shape table 0x895ec1/0x59df3c as 0x403d50/0x403c10 above), reads each footprint cell's own HEIGHT field (table 0x8a03e4 `+0x4` - not the shadow nibble `+0xe`) plus its neighbours, accumulates and divides by the sample count to get one flat target height, then writes that averaged height back into `+0x4` for 4 cells around each footprint corner - levelling the ground to one flat plane under the whole building. A type-indexed table (`0x5a7270`, bits `0x20000`/`0x40000`) adjusts the minimum averaging sample count per building type first. For types `0xd`/`0xe` specifically (boat huts, per `docs/unit_types`) a further gated 4-way jump table overrides 3 of the same 4 corner cells' `+0x4` height with the just-computed average offset by -1 on some corners - plausibly carving a one-step-lower boat ramp into the flattened pad; not live-confirmed. This is the actual terrain-flattening step of building placement - pop3-rev-analysis.md's building/construction write-up doesn't cite an address for this yet.

name: evict_building_occupant
role: `fn(building, specific_occupant_or_null) -> void`, traced this session (previously only referenced by role - "evicts everyone"/"evicts each occupant" - in several other rows, e.g. `0x406F40`, insect plague `0x510120`, never itself opened). Finds the occupant slot in the building's own 6-slot array (`+0x86`): the SPECIFIC one passed in if given (matched by its own cell-index field `+0x24`), else the FIRST occupied slot. Removes them: decrements the building's own occupancy count (`+0xA6`), clears that slot, clears a bit in `+0x9C`, and re-inserts the evicted person onto the land tile at the building's own position via `0x4D80E0` (`insert_unit_into_land_tile`, already cited in person_states.tsv row 5). Does NOT itself change the evicted person's own state - callers that want the "forced panic run" (burning building `0x408AB0`/`0x408B39`, insect-plague raid `0x510120`) do that separately, right after calling this. Building-side bookkeeping after the removal: if the evicted person was a preacher (type 4), ORs a per-tribe bitmask `0x96EACE` (not identified - plausibly an "alarm/defend" signal); if the building's own TYPE has bit `0x1` set in table `0x5A7270`, clears a busy flag (`+0x14` bit `0x1000`), zeroes `+0x9A`, and calls `0x408D20`/`0x40BBE0` (not traced) when that returns true; if the building's own TYPE has a nonzero threshold in a SECOND per-type table (`0x5A7248`), walks the REMAINING occupant slots up to that threshold and, for each one resolving to a live same-tribe unit (via `0x4077E0`, own row), sets a flag on it (`+0x76` bit `0x4`) - plausibly "wake up/reassign the others left inside", not confirmed.

`fn(word_id) -> unit_ptr_or_0`, traced this session (resolves `0x407490`'s own "not traced" reference to it). Resolves a word id through the global thing table (`0x890390`), returning 0 if the id is 0, the slot's own `+0xC` bit `0x1` (dead/removed) is set, or its `+0x2A` (class/type) is 0. This is the exact deduplicated form of the "resolve a reference-unit word field to a live pointer" pattern that appears re-inlined by hand at DOZENS of call sites across the exe (states 5/9/34/36's own per-unit `+0x72` reference checks, the insect-plague building scan, etc. - person_states.tsv) - most of those sites do NOT call this shared helper, they repeat the same 6 instructions themselves, so finding every caller of `0x4077E0` specifically undercounts how often this exact check is actually performed exe-wide.

building foundation check, runs every 4 turns per building (class_counter +0x2e mod 4 == 0), or every turn for a type flagged "water-sited" (type table 0x5A7228 +0x48 word, bit 15/byte+0x49&0x80 - boat huts 13/14 and anything else sharing the flag): recomputes the base height (+0x41) as the average height of the footprint's fine-grid cells (map-cell table 0x8A03E4 +0x4), skipped for a water-sited type which instead only clamps +0x41 up to a minimum of 1. For an ordinary (non-water-sited) type, instead counts how many footprint fine-cells are at or below sea level (height <= 0); if more than 5/8 (62.5%) of the footprint is submerged, destroys the building right away with sub-state 2 - this is the TODO's long-standing "second destroy reason (flooding?)", now traced as flooding, not steepness. Otherwise walks every footprint cell (skipping ones a unit stands on), comparing its height to the base - or to sea level 0, not the base, for a water-sited type's own footprint cells flagged as its water part - and either pulls it back towards that target by the type's rate (+0x44, 2/turn, via 0x44FDE0) or, the first time any single cell's absolute difference exceeds the type's tolerance (+0x46, 200, same for every type), destroys the building with sub-state 1 ("uneven ground") and stops checking further cells that call. Either destroy reason sets state 3 and fires the two destroy events (0x4ED6F0/0x4ED640) unless an instance flag (+0xe bit 0x10) suppresses them. Not part of this topic, not traced further: a water-sited type's own companion object (spawned/rechecked via 0x4ED8A0, type 0x53, at a neighbour cell through 0x40B860/0x4B9EF0 - looks like a dock/jetty, unrelated to destruction) and a per-occupant height resync via calc_point_height (0x44E940) at the end of the function.

`fn(building) -> bool`, traced this session (previously only referenced from `0x407490`'s own row as "not traced"). Returns false immediately if the building is now unoccupied (`+0xA6`==0, reached right after an eviction decrements it). Otherwise sums a per-occupant-TYPE "weight" (table `0x5A707F`, indexed by type) over up to the building's own per-type occupant-count threshold (table `0x5A7248`, the SAME table `0x407490`'s own post-eviction loop reads) for every occupant whose type differs from the building's own reference type (table `0x5A7228`+0x31, keyed by building type) - then returns true only if that summed weight is still <= the FIXED threshold `0x5A707F[building's own reference type]`. Reads as "does this building (by its weighted occupant mix) still have room/capacity for its primary purpose" - shares its table cluster with `0x40BBE0`'s own training-cost recompute (own row, confirmed near-identical occupant-weighting loop), and is exactly the gate `0x407490`'s own post-eviction bookkeeping uses to decide whether to call `0x40BBE0` and set `+0x9C` bit `0x80` - i.e. "after evicting someone, check if the building has capacity again, and if so, recompute its training cost/queue".

**Fully re-traced 2026-10-29, resolving the old stub.** `fn(building) -> void`, the generic per-turn building wear/decay/destruction tick - its ONLY caller is `unit_processing_class_2_bldg` (0x40347D), i.e. this runs every turn for every building. Bails if decay-immune (`+0x14` bit `0x80`). Every 4 turns (`class_counter +0x2E & 3 == 0`) decrements the wear accumulator `+0x9E` by 1 if nonzero (slow natural healing/cooldown between hits). Compares `+0x9E` against a per-building-TYPE threshold (table `0x5A7228`, stride 76, word at `+0x2E` i.e. absolute `0x5A7256` - **raw values this session: 2000 for nearly every buildable type, 16000 for the wall (type 10, 8x tougher), 22000 for the prison (type 19, despite the prison having a wood-cost of 0 below - so a prison CAN still be worn down by combat, just extremely slowly; the vault/library, type 18, has threshold 0, i.e. it never accumulates enough to need checking - genuinely indestructible by this path**); bails (nothing to do yet) if below threshold. Once at/above threshold: resolves the building's own wood-stock companion object (id word `+0x82`, via `0x890390`, same per-cell/per-building "stock object" reference `0x4980A0` also reads) and, if that type has flag `+0x4A` bit `0x8` set, force-zeroes the companion's own stock (`+0x96=0`) outright (an instant, non-gradual wipe for whichever building types carry that flag - not yet identified by type this session); otherwise calls **`0x4BA2C0(companion, -100)`** (own row - the master wood-stock/construction-stage adjuster) to remove one 100-wood chunk. If that adjuster reports a real stage change (`AL!=0`): evicts every occupant (`0x407490`, looped) when the wear is "serious" (the per-type damage value used upstream, `>= 3` after the `/4` scaling - i.e. only sufficiently strong hit-types evict) AND the building is occupied; spawns cosmetic damage smoke/sound-variance (`0x40B320`/`alloc_building_damage_smoke`, own row) when it returns a target; and shatters visible debris (`0x407860`, same mesh-shatter call the "uneven ground" destroy path uses) off the building. Then (regardless of the `AL` branch) re-arms the accumulator by subtracting the SAME per-type threshold from `+0x9E` (so a second hit's worth can accumulate again), spawns a smoke-variance/`0x4BA590`+`0x4BA5B0` pair (own rows) on the companion, and runs an "alert other same-tribe class-9 markers in range" sweep (unread this session - plausibly a town-defence/worker-rally signal, not confirmed). **Destruction**: checked right after the wood-stock reload - if the companion's own stock (`+0x96`) is now `<= 0`: makes ashes at the companion and deletes it (`0x40B230` then `0x4EF180`), tallies the building's own tribe's "destroyed building" stat (`0x41B550`, stat index 7) and deletes the building itself (`0x4EF180`) - **byte-for-byte the same ashes+stat+delete sequence as `0x40B130`** (Whirlwind's own destroy-via-wear finisher, own row), confirming combat/environmental wear-to-destruction and Whirlwind's wear-to-destruction converge on the identical final teardown, just reached via different front-ends (`0x409140`/`0x409200` vs `0x4980A0`). Finally plays UI sound `0x34` if the building's own construction-stage byte (`+0x78`, stale-but-harmless read even on the just-deleted path, since `0x4EF180` only tombstones the record rather than freeing memory immediately) is still `>0` - a "taking damage" cue on the surviving-but-hit path. **This is the exe's full "attacking/wearing down a building to destruction" mechanism**, resolving CONTEXT.md's "wear-down to destruction" and TODO.md's "no building damage yet" gap with concrete numbers - pop3-rev-analysis.md has no section yet to attach this to (no "Attacking a building: wear-down" write-up exists there today, only "Attacking a building"'s approach-order substates).

fn(kind, value, start, duration, extra): inserts a new 8-byte record `{kind:u8, extra:u8, value:i16, start:u16, duration:u16}` into a single GLOBAL (not per-tribe) sorted-by-`start` event table at `0x969BE2` (32 slots max, count byte `0x969BD3`, guarded off entirely once full or once a global "processing" flag `0x969BD7` bit 0 is set - gates at `0x969BD7`&1 and `0x969BD3<0x20`). Shared by the AI-script flyby's `FLYBY_SET_EVENT_*` channels AND (plausibly, not confirmed) other timed script/message events - this is a generic small scheduler, not flyby-specific by itself. Confirmed kinds this session: 1=POS, 2=ANGLE, 3=ZOOM, 4=INT_POINT, 5=TOOLTIP (own rows).

Per-turn driver for the global event table at `0x969BE2` (own row, `0x449240`): walks due entries (`start` reached per a global turn-ish counter `0x969BE0`, incremented once per call) and, for each due `kind`, calls that kind's "start" callback from a per-kind table at `0x59CD40`+kind*8 (own row group for kind=3/ZOOM: `0x449AE0` start, `0x449B30` tick, both own rows) with the event record pointer; marks the kind active in a bitmask `0x969BD6`. Every call, for the up-to-7 known kinds (0-6), re-invokes the per-kind "tick" callback at `0x59CD40`+kind*8+4 while that kind's active bit is set, clearing the bit once the callback reports done. The function's 2nd half (past `0x449544`) handles a SEPARATE, unrelated message-countdown timer (`0x969BD4`/`0x59CD3C`, random-jittered via the shared RNG-ish source `0x5CA850`) and a flyby-interrupt/cancel check (`0x89BBF7`==1) that tears down `0x89CE34`/`0x89CE35`/`0x89CE36` (the `0x417510`/own-row transition-counter state) and restores the camera - not fully traced. Feature scope beyond pure-flyby not confirmed; treat as the generic "scripted camera/message event" tick, not flyby-exclusive.

POS channel's "start" callback (kind 1, per-kind table at `0x59CD40`, see `0x449320`'s own row), run once per axis (x then z) when the event's `start` turn is reached. Converts the packed byte value for that axis from a 0-255 CELL index to world/render units via `(cell + 1) * 256` (confirms "Render units: 256 per cell", "Landscape projection") and reads the CURRENT focus value directly from `tribe_struct+0x24`(x)/`+0x26`(z) (confirmed fields). Computes the signed delta to the target with explicit WRAPAROUND handling on the 16-bit domain (shortest path across the map's wrap edge, not a plain subtraction) - confirms the world map wraps/is toroidal, at least in how the camera focus tracks it. Calls `0x44A070` (own row, generic ease-setup) once per axis with its own separate state block.

POS channel's "tick" callback (kind 1, see `0x449670`'s own row), every turn while active: advances two independent float accumulators (one per axis, same x87-float-ease style as the ZOOM channel's `0x449B30`) and writes the rounded result straight into `tribe_struct+0x24`(x)/`+0x26`(z) - confirms POS directly drives the camera focus position, nothing else. Does NOT touch `tribe_struct+0x2c` at any point. Also calls `0x4E9D70` with the x-axis accumulator (same helper `cam_pan_dolly`/`0x442920` calls for manual-drag panning - likely a generic "register this axis's last delta" utility, not traced further).

ANGLE channel's "start" callback (kind 2, see `0x449320`'s own row): reads the CURRENT yaw directly from `tribe_struct+0x32` (confirmed field, "Manual camera pan/rotate") and the event's target raw angle, then calls two angle-delta helpers (`0x4E9B70`/`0x4E9BA0`, not traced) to get both possible signed deltas (short way / long way around the 2048-unit circle) and picks between them based on a per-event direction-preference byte (the event record's `extra` field) - this is `ai-scripts.md`'s documented `FLYBY_SET_EVENT_ANGLE` "goes the shortest way" rule, now seen directly in code (with an explicit override flag, not unconditional). Sets up the ease via `0x44A070` the same way the other channels do; the tick callback (not traced this session) almost certainly writes the result back into `tribe_struct+0x32`, the same field the manual mouse-drag rotate function (`0x4429C0`) uses.

ZOOM channel's "start" callback (kind 3, table at `0x59CD40`, see `0x449320`'s own row), invoked once when the event's `start` turn is reached. Rescales the queued Q8.8 value to Q14 (`value <<= 6`, so 256(Q8,1.0)*64=16384(Q14,1.0) - the same 14-bit fixed point the camera rotation matrix uses, "Landscape projection"), then computes `target_delta = value - tribe_struct+0x34` (CONFIRMED: `tribe_struct+0x34` holds a live, signed Q14 "zoom channel" accumulator - corrects pop3-rev-analysis.md's old "+0x34, least certain, could be unrelated" candidate to confirmed) and calls `0x44A070(target_delta, duration, &0x969D52, &0x969D66)` (own row - a generic kinematic ease-setup shared by all flyby channels, now traced).

ZOOM channel's "tick" callback (kind 3, see `0x449320`/`0x449AE0` own rows), run every turn while the channel is active. Uses x87 float math to advance an accumulator at `0x969D5E` each tick (details of `0x44A070`'s own per-tick state at `0x969D52`/`0x969D5A`/`0x969D66` not fully re-derived), adds it onto `tribe_struct+0x34`, clamps the result to [-16384, +16384] (±1.0 in Q14) and writes it back - this is the live value live-memory captures would see if watching `+0x34` directly. Immediately calls `0x41C700(clamped_value, 0x4000)` (own row) every tick - the actual per-tick camera effect, NOT `tribe_struct+0x2c` (which `0x41C700` does not touch - see that row). Returns "done" once a global progress counter `0x969CEE` reaches the event's duration `0x969CF0`.

INT_POINT channel's "start" callback (kind 4, per-kind table at `0x59CD40`, see `0x449320`'s own row): reads the CURRENT camera focus (`tribe_struct+0x24`/`+0x26`, confirmed fields) and the event's target (x,z) cell (same `(cell+1)*256` conversion as `POS`, with the same 16-bit wraparound handling), computes the ANGLE from focus to target via the angle-from-vector helper `0x586074` (also used by `0x503550`'s building-sinks-in-water rocking and insect plague homing), then the signed delta from the CURRENT YAW (`tribe_struct+0x32`) to that angle via `0x4E9B70`/`0x4E9BA0` (same two helpers `ANGLE`'s own channel uses, own row) - this is a dynamic "turn the camera to look at this point" channel, continuously re-aimed (see `0x449D80`, its tick callback, which re-does the angle-to-target calculation every turn rather than easing toward a single fixed angle). Sets up the ease via `0x44A070`. **Level 1's own script never uses `FLYBY_SET_EVENT_INT_POINT`** (ai-scripts.md's usage count for it is 0/0) - confirmed not the mechanism behind anything observed in the `cam4.txt`/`cam5.txt` captures.

INT_POINT channel's "tick" callback (kind 4, see `0x449C40`'s own row): every turn, re-derives the angle from the CURRENT focus to the target point (not a fixed pre-computed angle - a live re-aim), eases toward it, and adds the result into `tribe_struct+0x32` (yaw, confirmed field) the same way the manual mouse-drag rotate function does, also setting the render-dirty bit `0x87CA1C`|=0x80. Confirmed: only ever touches yaw, never `tribe_struct+0x2c` or any distance-like field.

`fn(event_record)`, a tiny wrapper reading its own single argument as a 3-byte data record (category/`extra` at +1, packed x/z word at +2) and a global word (0x969CF8) before calling `0x44D7F0(category, word, global_word)` (own row). **Confirmed this session: this record IS the flyby's own `TOOLTIP` channel event** - `0x44A030` is that channel's "start" callback (kind 5, `0x449320`'s own row), called once at the event's `start` turn with the event record `0x449240` (own row) queued; the "category" is the script's `idx` argument remapped (0->1, 1->2). One-shot UI action, no continuous ease (no real "tick" behaviour; the shared tick slot `0x44A1E0` is also used by kind 6, not traced). The other confirmed caller of `0x44D7F0` is inline inside a level-script bytecode stepper (see that row) - a 2nd, not fully distinguished non-flyby script path to the same notification system.

`fn(delta: i32, duration: i32, state: *EaseState, out: *f32x2)` - the generic ease-setup helper every flyby channel's "start" callback calls (`0x449670`/`0x449920`/`0x449AE0`/`0x449C40`, own rows). Confirmed this session (traced statically, no live memory): `state` is a 0x14-byte per-channel blob carrying a persistent "current rate" field (read back across calls, not reset to zero each time - gives velocity continuity when an ease is re-triggered mid-motion) and `out` is literally `state+0x14` (confirmed from the ZOOM call site's own two pointers, `&0x969D52`/`&0x969D66`, which are exactly 0x14 apart) - one contiguous per-channel state block, not two separate ones. Computes a tick budget from `duration` scaled by the two literal constants at `0x58F2FC`/`0x58F300` (64.0 and 1/256, product = 0.25) floored at a minimum of 1.0 tick, then a kinematic "stopping distance" threshold from the carried-over rate (`rate^2 / (2*accel)`, classic constant-deceleration formula) and branches on whether `delta`'s magnitude is inside or outside that threshold: inside -> a single flat constant rate `delta/duration` (two of the output phase fields zeroed, i.e. a one-phase linear case); outside -> a two-phase accelerate/decelerate profile (duration split into a "time to kill the existing rate" piece and a remaining piece) - the exact blended formula for this second branch wasn't re-derived past that split. Matches `0x449B30`'s tick callback (own row) advancing a float accumulator from this same state block every turn. Generalizes across all flyby channels; not itself flyby-exclusive machinery (same style as the shared event-table scheduler, `0x449240`).

name: render_land_ui_1
role: Ghidra's own name. Per-frame renderer for the notification/tooltip record `0x44D7F0` (own row) writes - reads the active tribe's camera focus (`[0x74A350]+0x24`/`+0x26`) and, depending on `0x68C6C0` mode flags, either resolves the record's target unit or decodes its packed (x,z) cell via the same `(cell+1)<<8` conversion `POS`/`INT_POINT` use; offsets the label anchor sideways from the target via `move_pos_angle_length`/`0x4E6A70` at the camera's own yaw+90° (`[0x74A350]+0x32`); projects the result into screen space via `coord_global_convert`/`0x46DBE0` (the standard camera-matrix transform) and applies screen-origin offsets `0x87CA8C`/`0x87CA8E`. **Confirmed this session: pure screen-space label positioning - no write anywhere in this function to `tribe_struct+0x2c`, the render-block D field (`0x88F014`), or the `0x89CE34` transition counter.** Rules this function out too as the source of `+0x2c`'s flyby-time motion.

`fn(category, word_arg, dword_arg) -> false`. The shared "register a categorised notification" entry point: category 1-10 dispatches a jump table at 0x44DB20 into 10 case handlers, each writing a shared notification RECORD at `0x68B6A1`/`0x68C6A1..C0` (position word pair `+0x68C6BB`, a dword `+0x68C6A1`, a byte "kind" `+0x68C6C0`, a formatted text string via 0x55B5C0 with format-table `0x599970`) - this record is what `render_land_ui_1` (0x44A34D, own row) reads every frame to actually draw the popup (found this session - projects the record's world position through the standard camera matrix via `coord_global_convert`/0x46DBE0, offsets the label anchor point via `move_pos_angle_length`/0x4E6A70 at yaw+90°, applies screen-origin offsets `0x87CA8C`/`0x87CA8E` - **pure screen-space label positioning, no camera-distance or render-block write anywhere in it either**). Three ways in: (a) `fire_advisor_message_once`'s "recognised category" path (0x499F16, category 3-10); (b) directly from the level-SCRIPT interpreter - **confirmed this session**: the flyby's own `FLYBY_SET_EVENT_TOOLTIP` channel (kind 5, `0x449320`'s per-kind table) calls it via `0x44A030`, a tiny wrapper reading `category=byte[event_record+1]` (the event's `extra` field, remapped from the script's own `idx` argument: idx 0->category 1, idx 1->category 2) and `word_arg=byte[event_record+2..3]` (the packed x/z cell pair) straight from the queued event record - this is the confirmed mechanism behind `ai-scripts.md`'s `FLYBY_SET_EVENT_TOOLTIP x z idx start duration`; also reached inline inside a bytecode-stepping function at 0x490D05-0x490D28 (a second, non-flyby script path, category 1 or 2, not fully distinguished from (b)); (c) category 1/2 could in principle also be invoked directly by other in-engine code the same way, not just from script bytecode - not checked. Per-category behaviour: category 1 (0x44D861) walks a LINKED CHAIN of objects (class/type match 5/9, "head" scenery - docs/unit_types) via each object's own +0x20 "next" field, starting from a word at the caller's arg+0x6, until a head is found or the chain ends (then bails, no message); on success, builds the text from the found head's own +0x24 field - **this is almost certainly the "a building/pyramid is presented" behaviour reported for level 1's flyby**: a `TOOLTIP` keyframe with `idx=0` (level 1 has one, the 3rd) resolves to category 1, which walks to a "head"/monument-type scenery object near the given point and displays it; the other two level-1 tooltips (`idx=1`) use category 2, which resolves an object from a packed id (arg+0x8 & 0x3FF) and, if the object's tribe isn't 0xFF, additionally draws a 10-byte PER-TRIBE record from 0x8A035C + tribe*34 via 0x4539A0 - a tribe-coloured indicator, matching the "enemy-spell notice" guess elsewhere. Categories 3,5,6,7,8 (all share 0x44D9A9) bail if the LOCAL PLAYER's tribe has no living shaman (table 0x89DA65); else pick a per-category literal text id (0x256/0x258/0x258/0x258/0x259) - assorted "about your shaman" advisor tips, not combat alerts; none of these 5 is reached by any of the 11 known `fire_advisor_message_once` call sites, may be dead/unused in shipped levels. Categories 4 and 10 (shared, 0x44DA4F): no object lookup, generic text message at the MAP CENTRE (globals 0x87CAE2/0x87CAE4) - the two known call sites are "you can't go/build there" tips. Category 9 (0x44DAC6) reads a position-like global (0x973514) and a small counter (0x89BC26), then plays sound 0xE1 via 0x48A050 - matches the one known call site (0x4D9580). **Confirmed, this session: NEITHER this function NOR `render_land_ui_1` touches `tribe_struct+0x2c`, the render-block D field (0x88F014), or the `0x89CE34` transition counter anywhere** - the flyby's `TOOLTIP` channel (via this whole pipeline) does not move the camera. The timing correlation with `+0x2c`'s own motion (docs/camera.md "INT_POINT and TOOLTIP channels") is therefore NOT explained by this code path; if real, the cause is elsewhere.

name: calc_unit_shade_value
role: Computes the 0-15 shadow-intensity value landscape_move_1/landscape_set_unit_shadow write into a map-cell's +0xe low nibble. Takes the map-cell record pointer; reads a thing-index word at cell+0x8 (masked 0x3ff) into the global thing-pointer table 0x890390 - if that thing exists, isn't flagged `[+0xc] bit 0x1`, and its `unit_class` (+0x2a, same field "Blast push and flight"/unit-record docs already use) is non-zero (i.e. not an ordinary person/mobile sprite - ordinary people don't cast a baked ground shadow), it contributes a shadow amount: either a size-scaled one (`[+0x78]` scale/height field times a per-subtype signed byte from table 0x5a725d, /3) when the thing's `[+0x2c]` sub-kind is 1, or a flat per-subtype table 0x5a725d lookup otherwise. Then walks a SECOND, separate per-cell link (thing-index word at cell+0x6, same table 0x890390) as a linked list via each thing's own `+0x20` "next" field, summing a per-subtype table-0x5a79c3 contribution for every linked thing whose class (+0x2a) is 5, i.e. accumulating shadow from multiple stacked/overlapping objects on the same cell (buildings, trees, scenery) - clamped to a max of 15 (0xf) at every step and on return, matching the field's 4-bit width exactly. **Class 5 confirmed, 2026-10-29**: `docs/unit_types` directly confirms class 5 = scenery (trees 1-6, plants 7-8, head 9, fire 0xa, wood pile 0xb, reincarnation pillar 0xc, rock 0xd, portal 0xe, island 0xf, bridge 0x10, top/sub-level scenery 0x12/0x13) - the second-slot accumulation is literally "every scenery item stacked on this cell", not a tree-specific special case. **cell+0x8 vs cell+0x6 partially distinguished, same session, from read-site conventions across the whole exe (grepped every `0x8a03ec`/`0x8a03ea` - the two fields' literal addresses - in `dis.txt`, ~40+ distinct call sites each)**: every other reader of cell+0x6 (word) sign-extends it (`movsx`) before using it as a thing index - including `preacher_strike_scan`'s (0x43ABF0) OWN use of the SAME field (`table 0x8a03e4+0x6`) to scan person occupants of a cell - so +0x6 is a generic, shared, likely `-1`-terminated multi-class "occupant list head" walked via each thing's own `+0x20` next-pointer, reused by combat/AI scanning code as well as this shadow calc. Every reader of cell+0x8 instead treats it as UNSIGNED and several mask it `and/test ...,0x3ff` (this function included) - a packed word, not a plain index, and this function only ever checks ONE candidate from it (no `+0x20` chain walk) - consistent with +0x8 being a single "the one special/structural occupant" slot (a building or other map-fixture placeholder) as opposed to +0x6's general stack of everything else. name: interpret_script_upper
role: The statement-level PopScript interpreter (`IF`/`ELSE`/`ENDIF`/`EVERY`/`SET`/`INCREMENT`/`DECREMENT`/`MULTIPLY`/`DIVIDE` grammar, `ai-scripts.md`'s `stmt`/`cond` rules) - evaluates ONE statement per call, dispatching on the next bytecode word via a small jump table at `0x48c960` (range 0x3f4-0x3fd, i.e. tokens 1012-1021: the 6 comparison operators plus `AND`/`OR`, reached while evaluating an `IF`'s condition chain through `0x48f130`/`0x48f230`, neither traced this session) for conditions, a dedicated block at `0x48c844` for `EVERY`, and falls through toward the end (`0x48c8e3`) to call `interpret_script` (`0x48CC60`, own row) when the statement is a `DO` command. **`EVERY n [m]` fully resolved this session, settling `ai-scripts.md`'s own flagged-open question** ("the EVERY off-by-one and whether there is a per-tribe phase"): resolves the optional offset operand `m` through the normal field resolver `0x48F350` (defaulting via the grammar's own "second F present iff next word isn't BEGIN" rule), reads the period operand's raw stored field VALUE directly (not through the resolver - confirming `ai-scripts.md`'s "both operands must be constants"), computes `turn(0x89D188, the global current-turn counter) + target_struct's own signed byte at +0xc22 ("tribe_num" per backup.xml) + m`, then does a plain bitwise `test period_value, that_sum` (zero flag = "fire this turn"). Since `ai-scripts.md` already established the stored period value IS `period-1` (a power-of-two-minus-one bitmask), `test mask, x` is bit-for-bit equivalent to `x & mask == 0`, i.e. `(turn + tribe_num + m) % period == 0` - **exactly the formula `ai-scripts.md` guessed the Reincarnated Lua converter might add on top of the original ("whether the original does this is unknown") - confirmed here, in the original exe itself, using `tribe_num` (not a hardcoded tribe colour constant) as the per-tribe phase.** On a firing turn, calls `0x48c980` (own row) to run the nested block; otherwise skips it via a `BEGIN`/`END`-balanced scan (`0x48c7e1` onward, reused identically by `IF`'s own false-branch skip). **Possible connection, not confirmed**: `tribe+0xc22`/`tribe_num` is also read by `process_tribe_cmd` (`0x40bce0`'s row) as an unexplained "TYPE argument" valued `4` in that context - plausibly the same field misused/reused there, worth re-checking now that this session has pinned down what `+0xc22` normally holds.

`interpret_script_upper`'s (own row) "run a nested block" helper: consumes the `BEGIN` token (bails early, `0x48cc07`, if the very next word is already `END` - an empty block) then loops calling back into the statement dispatcher for each statement until it hits `END` (not traced instruction-by-instruction beyond confirming the recursive structure - this is the `block := BEGIN stmt* END` grammar rule). Called from 3 sites so far: `IF`'s true branch, `IF`'s `ELSE` branch, and `EVERY`'s body when it fires (`interpret_script_upper`'s own row).

Takes one argument (`[esp+0x44]`, a rect descriptor: left/top/width/height at +0x37/+0x3B/+0x47/+0x4B), converts it to screen pixels via `parameterize_by_screen_width`/`_height` (0x44A1F0/0x44A210) and draws the bar's frame art first via `draw_hfx_ingame_window(rect, sprite=0x5CA9E0)` (0x4A1F50). **Fill-value formula**: reads `eta = tribe+0x961` (a field this session also newly traced - see 0x41A590/0x41A850's own note: computed from `SPELL_<spell>_OPT_S` × a game-speed-ish byte (0x89D161) ÷ (0x5AA44C+1), × the candidate spell's cost ÷ `find_spell_for_advisor`'s returned share, i.e. an "advisor's estimated turns/mana-rate to finish charging the tracked spell" bookkeeping value - matches pop3-rev-analysis.md's "Charges and mana" aside that `SPELL_<X>_OPT_S` is read only by "the advisor's mana bookkeeping", now pinned to this exact computation and consumer). **Found/traced this session (via `landscape_move_1`'s own call site `0x4BA37D`), the master wood-stock/construction-stage primitive - the single most load-bearing function in the whole building-lifecycle picture.** `fn(stock_companion, delta) -> bool changed`: adds `delta` (a signed count of raw wood units, always ±100 at every call site found) into the companion object's own stock word (`+0x96`), then resolves the companion's OWNING building (id word `+0x92`, via `0x890390`) - if none, just applies the raw delta and returns. Otherwise, using a per-building-TYPE "full wood cost" threshold (table at `type*76+0x5A7242`, i.e. absolute field `+0x1A` of the already-known 76-byte-stride building-type table `0x5A7228` - **raw values this session: 300 for all 3 hut sizes, 900 tower/temple, 1100 spy-hut/fire-hut, 800 warrior-hut/reconversion, 200 wall, 500 gate/"type 12", 1100 all 4 vehicle huts, 0 guard/vault/prison**), recomputes the building's own **construction/wear STAGE byte (`+0x78` - the SAME field `calc_unit_shade_value` reads as a height/size multiplier for shadow purposes, doubling as "how built does this instance look")**: stage `4` ("fully built/operational") once stock `>=` threshold - firing the standard state-transition pair into **class-2 state `2`** (confirmed building-state value: "operational", distinct from the state-3 "being destroyed" finalize `0x406F40`'s own target state) unless suppressed (`+0xE` bit `0x10`); else, while stock `>0`, stage `= clamp((stock*4-1)/(threshold-1), 0, 3)` - the literal 0-3 fractional-build formula behind buildings.md's own "more and more parts of the real model show" description; else (stock `<=0`) stage `=0` ("bare/blueprint") and a local "depleted" flag is set. Any stage CHANGE triggers a shadow-footprint recompute (`landscape_move_1`, 0x403A00 - explains why this wood-stock function calls a terrain-shadow function) and mirrors the new stage byte onto a SECOND linked companion (`+0x94` on the building, role not identified - possibly a secondary visual/LOD object) if one resolves. On a POSITIVE delta (repair/construction, never on a negative/wear delta): clears a damage/scorch-type byte on the companion (`+0xA0=0xFF`) and on the building (`+0xAF=0xFF`) - repairing/rebuilding erases any lingering "what destroyed the last version" marker. Returns whether a stage transition actually happened (checked by callers `0x4092A0`/combat-wear and `0x4980A0`/Whirlwind to decide whether to run their own visible destruction-effect tails). **This single function is the exe's entire "how does a building visually grow during construction and crumble during wear/dismantling" state machine** - no `pop3-rev-analysis.md` "Building construction"/"Dismantling" section exists yet to attach it to; open-populous's own `buildings.md` "Dismantling"/"Building it" sections describe an UNVERIFIED, independently-designed `[ours]` state machine (`GameMap::dismantle_step`/`dismantle_piece`, a per-piece "pull one wood piece, nothing fetched" toggle) that should be checked against this real 0-4 stage/threshold formula in a follow-up `original-game-spec` pass - in particular, **the exe formula here has NO evidence of a player-facing "Dismantle" toggle/order at all**: every confirmed caller of `0x4BA2C0` is either normal construction (positive delta, not traced to its own caller this session) or WEAR/DESTRUCTION (`0x4092A0` combat, `0x4980A0` Whirlwind) - open-populous's own friendly "switch a built building to Dismantle, it gives wood back piece by piece" feature has no confirmed exe counterpart found so far; it may be a legitimate original mechanic reached through a caller not yet found (a construction UI command, unexamined), or it may be an open-populous invention - worth a dedicated search for a player "dismantle" order/command before trusting buildings.md's section as faithful.

**The "patrol points, up to 8" mechanism (shortcuts.md: Ctrl+Alt+left click with followers), traced this session.** `fn(tribe, is_unit_target, pos_or_unit_ref, ...)`, called from `process_tribe_cmd` (0x440857, confirmed - falls inside that function's own already-documented 0x43E8E0-0x442480 range): bails if a per-tribe gate (`tribe+0x931`) is unset or the per-tribe patrol-point COUNTER (`tribe+0xC5C`) is already >= 8 - **the literal "up to 8" cap**. Picks kind 6 ("go near X") with a target computed from a referenced unit's own packed position, or kind 0xB (11, the already-documented "join/hold a melee ring" order, reused here for a unit-targeted point) with a target passed directly, depending on the caller's own boolean (plausibly "clicked on a unit vs. open ground"). Walks the tribe's own `person_units` list; for each unit passing a flag check (`+0x7A` bit 0x80, plausibly "currently selected" - matching "with followers" in the UI): **on the very first point of a sequence (`tribe+0xC5C == 0`), first calls `0x436CA0` to wipe that unit's entire prior order state** (a fresh patrol list); allocates ONE shared group (shared across every matching unit, allocated once outside the per-unit loop) with the chosen kind/target; **assigns it into secondary slot `tribe+0xC5C`** (NOT slot 0, and NOT wiped first on subsequent calls) for every matching unit. After the whole tribe pass, increments `tribe+0xC5C`. **This is the confirmed, genuine exception to "everything always uses secondary slot 0"**: repeated calls (one per Ctrl+Alt+click) populate DISTINCT secondary slots (0, 1, 2, ... up to 7) on the same units without clobbering earlier ones, and `order_advance`'s own already-documented round-robin scan (starting right after the cursor, wrapping at 8) is what then makes the unit cycle through all of them in sequence, repeating once it wraps back past slot 0 - this is the actual "patrol/guard between markers" implementation, not `guard_control_units` (see pop3-rev-analysis.md "Command groups" and the Guard controller note). **The unit-vs-ground boolean, the `+0x931` gate, and the `+0xC5C` reset are now all resolved (later session)**: `tribe+0x931` is a per-tribe running count of currently-selected units (maintained elsewhere, incremented per selected unit found - same `+0x7A` bit 0x80 flag this function itself reads), so the gate is simply "does this tribe have at least one unit selected right now." `tribe+0xC5C` is reset to 0 by exactly one other place in the whole exe - a tiny, standalone command case inside this SAME `process_tribe_cmd`, whose entire body is "load the tribe, zero `+0xC5C`" (almost certainly shortcuts.md's `N: release the held followers`) - no other code resets it, confirming the counter is genuinely per-TRIBE state that persists across unrelated unit selections, not reset per-selection. The bool branch: the bool==0 (kind 6/move) path's own "unit" argument is, at its one confirmed call site, a BRAND-NEW class-9 object the caller just allocated at the clicked ground position (`alloc_unit(class=9,...)`, through the same pending-handoff pipeline used for spirits/melee companions) - i.e. a ground click is secretly "go near this throwaway marker unit", not a raw position; the bool==1 (kind 0xB/11) path's argument is a real, pre-existing unit id passed directly from `process_tribe_cmd`, confirming a unit click really does mean "attack this unit" (kind 11's own already-documented sub-state 0 unconditionally calls `attack_order_handler`, exiting having done nothing - and so retrying every tick - on failure). Full behavioural write-up, address-free: `docs/specs/units.md` "Patrol orders".

name: compute_cell_light
role: Per-cell landscape-texture brightness byte (map-cell +0xd, table 0x8a03e4): `clamp((sunBase + dz*sunZ - dx*sunX)/350 + (low_nibble(+0xe)+8)*16, 0, 255)` where dx/dz are height deltas to the cell's own +2 neighbours and sunX/sunZ/sunBase are the level's sun vector (0x937aa8/0x937aaa/0x937aac); called from level_land_processing_2 (0x44df40) per dirty cell after every height edit, so it tracks terrain edits live, not baked once at load - resolves the map-cell +0xe low nibble's previously-unidentified role. Live-measured this session on two running levels (on-disk Inclination 0x40 and 0x20, both ShadeStart=28/ShadeRange=15): sunX=sunZ=sunBase=**147 in both**, confirming (with 0x401040) this is the flat hardcoded constant, not derived per-level - open-populous's `SunParams::from_sunlight` guess (180/225/280, varying by ShadeRange/ShadeStart) has no basis; the right fix is a flat 147/147/147 unless 0x401350's gated day/night tick turns out to be active in some game mode. Flat cells (dx=dz=0) read light=128 exactly live, matching `clamp(147/350 + 128, 0, 255)` with the 147/350 term flooring to 0. A live spot-check on sloped cells did NOT reproduce the formula from a naive `base+(z*128+x)*16` cell-address read (see dis.txt around 0x4be259/0x4be261: the packed-index build masks x/z with `0xFE`/`0xFE00` before scaling, which a plain row-major address calc does not reproduce bit-for-bit) - attributed to that addressing gap in the one-off measurement script, not the formula, which the disassembly confirms matches the existing doc exactly. First pass 2026-10-20 claimed the masking was inert and a plain height(x,z)/height(x+2,z) (real 0..127 coords) reproduced it bit-for-bit - WRONG, caught and corrected same session. role: `fn(self)`, found this session (Ghidra-named, not previously catalogued) - the Hypnotism spell effect object's own per-tick body. Reuses `self+0x6C` as a plain tick counter (not its usual "max life" meaning for a class-1 person - this is a class-6-ish spell-effect object, different field layout). `fn(candidate, caster_tribe) -> bool`, found this session - the Hypnotism radius-scan's own eligibility predicate (passed to 0x515E30 from 0x50EA60). True only if: candidate is class 1 (person); type is NOT 7 (shaman), 8 (angel), or 1 (wildman); `candidate+0x10` bit 0x1000 (the already-documented "invisible" status) is clear; AND either the candidate's tribe differs from `caster_tribe` (an ordinary target), OR it already equals `caster_tribe` but the candidate is already mid-hypnotism-countdown with `+0xAC==0` (the "already captured, re-hit to refresh/finish" case 0x50EB00 itself handles specially). Matches the documented Hypnotism rule exactly ("not wildmen, shamans, angels") plus the invisibility exclusion, which the narrative description doesn't mention.

`fn(self, target_tribe) -> void`, found this session (action callback for Hypnotism's radius scan, called via 0x515E30 from 0x50EA60/process_hypnotism) - **the actual generic "this person now belongs to target_tribe" primitive, kill-and-replace rather than an in-place tribe write, same idiom as "Preacher conversion"'s own success path**. If `self+0x10` bit 0x800 (the already-documented GHOST status) is set: just `delete_unit` (0x4EF180) outright, no replacement - **this is the exe-level implementation of "Per spell" 7's own "Ghosts are destroyed"**, and almost certainly also explains the long-open `+0x11`/`+0x10` bit-0x800 "exemption" behaviour independently found this session in preacher_strike_scan (bails if the STRIKER is a ghost), `0x4D4B50` (spawns a special death effect for a ghost), and `0x4D83B0`'s `0x4D850C` branch (destroys a ghost CANDIDATE with no replacement on a successful roll) - all four are the same underlying "a ghost has no real body to hand off" rule, not four unrelated mysteries.
